content.content:
(* An integer power answers its base's own type; at a negative exponent the bases 1 and -1 give their exact power, a base of 0 throws DivisionByZero, and any other base throws IntegerOverflow, at an exponent of every integer type. *)
component IntegerPowerContractWalk
export Executable

overflows(f: () -> Any): Boolean =
  try
    ignore(f())
    false
  catch e
    IntegerOverflow => true
  end

dividesByZero(f: () -> Any): Boolean =
  try
    ignore(f())
    false
  catch e
    DivisionByZero => true
  end

shown(v: Any): String =
  typecase v of
    IntLiteral => v.asString || " : IntLiteral"
    ZZ32 => v.asString || " : ZZ32"
    ZZ64 => v.asString || " : ZZ64"
    NN32 => v.asString || " : NN32"
    NN64 => v.asString || " : NN64"
    ZZ => v.asString || " : ZZ"
    QQ => v.asString || " : QQ"
    RR64 => v.asString || " : RR64"
    else => v.asString || " : another type"
  end

negativeZZ32(): () = do
    two: ZZ32 = 2
    zero: ZZ32 = 0
    one: ZZ32 = 1
    mone: ZZ32 = -1
    assert(overflows(fn () => two^(-1)), "ZZ32 2^(-1) is no integer and throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(dividesByZero(fn () => zero^(-1)), "ZZ32 0^(-1) throws DivisionByZero; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(one^(-1)), "1 : ZZ32", "ZZ32 1^(-1) is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(-1)), "-1 : ZZ32", "ZZ32 (-1)^(-1) is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(-2)), "1 : ZZ32", "ZZ32 (-1)^(-2) is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(two^3), "8 : ZZ32", "ZZ32 2^3 is the ZZ32 8; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
  end

negativeZZ64(): () = do
    two: ZZ64 = widen(2)
    zero: ZZ64 = widen(0)
    one: ZZ64 = widen(1)
    mone: ZZ64 = widen(-1)
    assert(overflows(fn () => two^(-1)), "ZZ64 2^(-1) is no integer and throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(dividesByZero(fn () => zero^(-1)), "ZZ64 0^(-1) throws DivisionByZero; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(one^(-1)), "1 : ZZ64", "ZZ64 1^(-1) is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(-1)), "-1 : ZZ64", "ZZ64 (-1)^(-1) is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(-2)), "1 : ZZ64", "ZZ64 (-1)^(-2) is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(two^3), "8 : ZZ64", "ZZ64 2^3 is the ZZ64 8; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
  end

negativeNN32(): () = do
  end

fractions(): () = do
    assert((2/3)^(-1), 3/2, "a rational base gives the fraction: (2/3)^(-1) is 3/2; numbers.tex, section \"Rational Numbers\", opr ^")
    assert(2.0^(-1), 0.5, "a floating-point base gives the fraction: 2.0^(-1) is 0.5")
  end

exponentTypes(): () = do
    two: ZZ32 = 2
    zero: ZZ32 = 0
    one: ZZ32 = 1
    mone: ZZ32 = -1
    assert(shown(two^(widen(3))), "8 : ZZ32", "a ZZ64 exponent; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(two^(unsigned(3))), "8 : ZZ32", "an NN32 exponent; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(two^(widen(unsigned(3)))), "8 : ZZ32", "an NN64 exponent; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(two^(big(3))), "8 : ZZ32", "a ZZ exponent; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown((big(2))^(big(3))), "8 : ZZ", "a ZZ base and a ZZ exponent; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(overflows(fn () => two^(big(-1))), "ZZ32 2 to a ZZ -1 throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    huge: ZZ = (big(2))^70
    hugeOdd: ZZ = huge + big(1)
    assert(shown(zero^huge), "0 : ZZ32", "0 to an exponent beyond 64 bits is 0; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(one^huge), "1 : ZZ32", "1 to an exponent beyond 64 bits is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^huge), "1 : ZZ32", "-1 to an even exponent beyond 64 bits is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^hugeOdd), "-1 : ZZ32", "-1 to an odd exponent beyond 64 bits is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(overflows(fn () => two^huge), "2 to an exponent beyond 64 bits throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^, opr-overview.tex, subsection \"Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators\"")
    assert(dividesByZero(fn () => zero^(-huge)), "0 to a negative exponent beyond 64 bits throws DivisionByZero; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(overflows(fn () => two^(-huge)), "2 to a negative exponent beyond 64 bits throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(-hugeOdd)), "-1 : ZZ32", "-1 to an odd negative exponent beyond 64 bits is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown((big(-1))^hugeOdd), "-1 : ZZ", "a ZZ -1 to an odd exponent beyond 64 bits is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(overflows(fn () => (big(3))^huge), "a ZZ 3 to an exponent beyond 64 bits throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^, opr-overview.tex, subsection \"Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators\"")
    maxL: ZZ64 = 9223372036854775807
    twoTo63U: NN64 = unsigned(maxL) + unsigned(widen(1))
    assert(shown(zero^twoTo63U), "0 : ZZ32", "an NN64 exponent of 2^63 is positive: 0 to it is 0; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^twoTo63U), "1 : ZZ32", "-1 to the even NN64 2^63 is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown(mone^(twoTo63U + unsigned(widen(1)))), "-1 : ZZ32", "-1 to the odd NN64 2^63+1 is -1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    twoTo31: ZZ64 = widen(2147483647) + widen(1)
    assert(overflows(fn () => (big(3))^twoTo31), "a ZZ 3 to an exponent beyond the int's range throws IntegerOverflow; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^, opr-overview.tex, subsection \"Multiplication, Division, Modulo, and Remainder Operators\"")
    assert(shown((big(-1))^twoTo31), "1 : ZZ", "a ZZ -1 to the even exponent 2^31 is 1; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
    assert(shown((big(0))^twoTo31), "0 : ZZ", "a ZZ 0 to the exponent 2^31 is 0; basic-integers.tex, section \"Integers\", opr ^")
  end

run(): () = do
    negativeZZ32()
    negativeZZ64()
    negativeNN32()
    negativeNN64()
    negativeZZ()
    numeralType()
    fractions()

content.content:
## In short

- **The six sites have three causes, not two.** On the shared library text of the error and zero contracts, the distance falls from 49 to 44. Five sites clear: `QQ`'s four and `strToFloat`'s. `strToInt`'s site keeps its exact text: "ZZ32->ZZ32 is not applicable to an argument of type Any". Its body is the `if d <- digit(…) then d radix^(n-i) else fail(…) end` of a `SUM[\ZZ32\]`, and `fail[\T\]`'s result-only `T` there takes its bound `Any`. Writing `fail[\ZZ32\]` on top of the patch takes the distance to 43, and nothing else moves. So that site needs both the power's own type and the typed `fail`.
- **Uses.**
  - Walk's suite reaches 79 distinct integer-base power sites, with 3,324 calls. All 11 sites that see a negative exponent are in three tests present since the record's first commit: `realArith`, `compoundArray` and `simpleExp`. Each writes a decimal scale as `10^(-k)`.
  - Every other value already is the integer: the natives answer it, and only the declared type says `RR64` (row 438).
  - microGPT has no integer-base power of its own. It reaches one through `strToInt` while it parses the exponents of its data (`explorations/run-c4/src/FlatData.fss:34`, `explorations/apl/mg/FlatData2.fss:37`), always at a nonnegative exponent.
- **Per contract** (the 49 are the last landed gate, `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-15b/gate/distance.txt`):

| contract | sites cleared of the six | distance | walk's 26 power tests | microGPT quick pair | library text |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E, an error (`IntegerOverflow`; `DivisionByZero` at 0; ±1 exact) | 5, and 6 with `fail[\ZZ32\]` | 44 (43) | 23 pass; 3 team tests fail | all pass, every value line equal to the base | 15 edits, +29/−27 lines, and 11 lines of walk natives |
| Z, zero (truncated toward 0; `DivisionByZero` at 0; ±1 exact) | as E | as E (same text) | 24 pass; 2 team tests fail, and `compoundArray`'s output moves in 6 lines | as E | as E |
| R, a rational, typed by the exponent (the Working Draft's split) | 4 (`QQ`'s); `strToFloat`'s stays, now typed `QQ`; 2 new | 46 | 10 pass; 16 fail | both stop in `strToInt` | 21 edits, +91/−29 |
| X, an exponent typed so that it cannot be negative (`NN32`, `NN64`, a numeral) | 5, with the two library callers converted | 43 (with the run-to-run `LEXICO` site gone) | 10 pass; 16 fail by "Ambiguous coercion" | all pass, every value line equal to the base | 23 edits, +57/−31 |

- **The designers' later word holds a negative case.** Guy Steele's `simpleIntArith.intToIntPower` (snapshot `2eb54ef20`, 2011-11-17), bound nowhere, answers 0 for a negative exponent. Called directly, it gives 0 at a base of 2 and at a base of 0, 1 at a base of 1, and raises at every negative base, (−1)^(−1) included. So it is the zero contract with two slips (section 7).
- **Peers.**
  - Julia raises `DomainError`, except at bases ±1. For a numeral exponent it gives a float.
  - Rust types the exponent `u32`.
  - Swift has no integer power.
  - X10 has no power operator. Its `Math.pow(Int, Int)` answers a `Double`.
  - The revival's own precedent: walk refuses a negative exponent in a size (F-222).
- **History.**
  - Jan-Willem Maessen typed the interpreter's integer powers `RR64` on 2008-06-03 (c07ae816b, bfe7a5ced). They had been `Number`. At the time every integer was an `RR64` (`trait Integral extends { StandardTotalOrder[\Integral\], RR64 }`).
  - Guy Steele widened the exponent to `AnyIntegral` and wrote `QQ`'s power on 2008-07-21 (dc41d5000).
  - The revival's flat tower (d846e3644, 2026-09-27) made `RR64` a sibling of the integers, and from then on the declared type no longer holds the integer value.
